Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 2 days of central lower abdominal pain with feeling hot/sweaty, mild nausea, urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine.
- Clinician impression: suspected urinary tract infection; 3-day antibiotic course prescribed with safety-net advice.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Lower abdominal pain with urinary symptoms
  - Timeline: 2 days of central lower abdominal pain.
  - Associated symptoms: feeling hot/sweaty; mild nausea; increased urinary frequency; pink-tinged urine (hematuria); increased thirst.
  - Pertinent negatives: no vomiting; no dysuria initially; no back pain; no vaginal discharge; no epigastric pain/reflux; no diarrhea. Constipated last week, now resolved; stool normal; no blood in stool.
  - Menstrual/gynecologic: regular periods; no intermenstrual bleeding; no postcoital bleeding. Previously had an internal contraceptive implant; no longer in place.
  - Travel: no recent travel abroad.
  - Examination/vitals: self-reported temperature ~37°C one hour prior.
  - Clinical impression: suspected urinary tract infection (UTI).
  - Plan discussed: 3-day antibiotic course (twice daily). Safety-net: seek care if worsening abdominal pain, high fever, back pain, new/worsening symptoms, or recurrence; may require face-to-face assessment.

Issue 2:
- Medication allergy
  - Amoxicillin allergy reported.

Issue 3:
- Social history context
  - Lives with parents.
  - Alcohol: drinks beer about 1 drink, approximately 4 times per week.
  - Non-smoker.

Medications:
- No regular prescription medications reported.
- No over-the-counter medications reported.
- Antibiotic for suspected UTI: name/dose/route not documented; prescribed twice daily for 3 days.

Allergies:
- Amoxicillin.

Past Medical History:
- No significant past medical history reported.
- Prior internal contraceptive implant; currently not using it.

Social History:
- Lives with parents.
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: ~1 beer per occasion, ~4 times/week.
- Family history: mother with breast cancer (early stage, treated).

Preventative History:
- Cervical screening test: not discussed.
- Mammogram: not discussed.
- Prostate blood test: not applicable/not discussed.
- Fecal occult blood test: not discussed.
- Bone mineral density: not discussed.
- Vaccination status: not discussed.
- Recent optometry/skin check/other preventive visits: not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: self-reported temperature 37°C about one hour prior.
- No in-person physical examination performed (telehealth).

Plan:
- Send antibiotic prescription to patient’s allocated pharmacy; patient to start as soon as available.
- Take antibiotics twice daily for 3 days (agent/dose/route not documented).
- Safety-net: contact clinic urgently if abdominal pain worsens, fever develops, back pain occurs, new symptoms arise, or if no improvement; may require face-to-face evaluation.
- Advise to seek care if symptoms recur.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: urine dipstick/urinalysis and culture not performed; pregnancy status and last menstrual period not documented; sexual history/STI risk not assessed; analgesia and hydration advice not provided; specific antibiotic name/dose/route not documented; drug interaction review not documented.
- Internal conflicts: patient denied dysuria earlier, but later acknowledged “a little bit of difficulty when passing urine” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: some unclear/inaudible segments and brief communication barriers; overall key clinical details captured.
